The Selvatico 1722 letters were not among the links and were not viewed.
seen.extent: 31 May 1721: about 12 lines of dot-separated numbers inside clear Italian. 20 Mar 1726: whole letter c. 21r-22v mostly in number groups (about 70 lines, groups 1-330) with clear Italian lines between. 19 Feb 1727: clear French with one run of about 6 lines of numbers on c. 23r. 27 Feb 1726: the number runs carry an INTERLINEAR decipherment written above them (cc. 5-6) and the same closing group 4.115.33.326.
seen.cipher: Numeric nomenclator with dot-separated groups from 1 to about 330 (single-letter values and word codes, underlined groups for nulls or code words). The 27 Feb 1726 interlinear readings supply the key for the same code, and the 20 Mar 1726 and 19 Feb 1727 letters carry the same closing group 4.115.33.326, so they are in the same system and are not ciphertext-only.

title: Düben to Queen Lovisa Ulrika, system B ('Chiffer n:o 2'), 1764
correspondents: C.W. von Düben / N.P. Gyldenstolpe → Queen Lovisa Ulrika (and each other)
shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Kungliga arkiv, Drottning Lovisa Ulrika, Utgångna skrivelser, SE/RA/710003/02/008/b/K 259, images 118-124
folio_note: 223 images online (IIIF A0073297). Image 107: a full page of 3-digit numeric cipher (groups 17-720, dot-separated) facing a French clear page mentioning the Empress, Saldern; several more all-cipher pages around images 60-125 in a sampled contact sheet; images ~216-220 a folder "Chiffernycklar" and three key tables.
status: Catalogue: "Drottning Lovisa Ulrikas hemliga korrespondens. Brev från C.W. von Düben till N.P. Gyldenstolpe och Lovisa Ulrika 1764-1765 ... Chiffernycklar." Not on DECODE (no Lovisa Ulrika record), not in the repo. No decipherment seen on the sampled pages; interlinear decipherment not checked page by page. The 24 Oct Riksarkivet sweep listed K 259 as keys only; the 26 Oct sample (image 107) shows a full page of numeric cipher. 27 Oct 2026, Brice Dudout (email): Frederick II's letter of 3 March 1765 in this group is printed in the Politische Correspondenz, vol. 24, no. 15458 (one letter; Düben's code letters unaffected; targets/duben1764/). why: The queen's private cipher channel during the 1764-66 Hat/Cap crisis and her dealings with Russia and Prussia; the keys sit in the same volume, so it should read quickly.

Published key applies, not tried: not digitised.
